structure: Part 1, the whole ruling file: every one of the 23 lines of workareas/shared/design-release-2-1/sources/ruling-sam-2026-11-10.md, read word for word. The file is the standard ruling shape: an H1 ('Ruling: Sam, 10 November 2026'), a two-line setting note (lines 3-4) saying Sam decided these while reviewing what in the waiting-on-design theme could be built before the session with the new interaction designer, one six-line verbatim blockquote of Sam's own words (lines 6-11), then '## Decided' (line 13) with three numbered items (lines 15-18, 19-21, 22-23), each a bold decision sentence followed by the main session's reading of it. The blockquote covers four topics: germline (germinal) products not suiting the waiting-on-design theme and matching in with animals as the reference point for everything; folding the Germinals date calendar into one of the Germinals rows rather than leaving it separate; commodities search being handled by a different ticket with its call blocked until that ticket is implemented; and no confirmation being needed when a transit country is added to or removed from a table, closing with the rhetorical question 'What confirmation do you need other than it was there, now it isn't, or it wasn't there, now it is?'. Each Decided item was checked phrase by phrase against the blockquote: a fact the blockquote says in so many words is recorded verbatim quoting the blockquote, and a fact only the Decided list carries (inc-192, inc-053, inc-014, the MOJ date picker, the 9 November interaction designer ruling, the 'without JavaScript' qualifier) is recorded inferred, quoting the Decided item, with the statement and note saying what in the blockquote implies it and where the blockquote is silent. The part covered: the whole blockquote phrase by phrase, all three Decided items in full, the setting note's authority framing, the report design questions and conflicts each item answers (design question 12 / c-283 on the germinal date calendar, design question 3 / c-012 on commodity results as you type, design question 4 / c-006 on transit countries in place), and six gap claims for the points the ruling touches but leaves open. There are no tables, images, appendices or linked files in this source, and nothing in it belongs to another part.

claims.statement: Germinal (germline) products do not belong in the waiting-on-design theme.
claims.quote: I don't think germline suits being in the waiting-on-design thing.
claims.note: Sam says 'germline'; the backlog and the Decided list call the set germinal products. Restated as the bold sentence of Decided item 1.

claims.statement: The germinal pages take live animals as their reference point for everything.
claims.ref: ruling-sam-2026-11-10.md blockquote, lines 6-7; restated in Decided item 1
claims.quote: Germlines will just match in with animals as a reference point for everything.
claims.note: Decided item 1 restates it as 'The germinal pages take live animals as their reference for everything.' Recorded once, because both say the same fact.

claims.statement: The Germinals date calendar is folded into one of the rows on Germinals.
claims.quote: If anything, fold this in the Germinals date calendar into one of the rows on Germinals,
claims.note: Sam prefixes it 'If anything', so the quote puts the fold as the option he would take rather than an absolute instruction; Decided item 1 records it as decided.

claims.statement: The Germinals date calendar does not suit being a separate item of work.
claims.quote: but that doesn't suit being separate.

claims.statement: Commodities search is handled by a different ticket, not by this work.
claims.ref: ruling-sam-2026-11-10.md blockquote, line 8; restated as the bold sentence of Decided item 2
claims.quote: Commodities search is being handled by a different ticket.
claims.note: Decided item 2's bold sentence restates it as 'Commodity search is handled by a separate ticket.' Recorded once, because both say the same fact.

claims.statement: The design call on commodities search is blocked until the different ticket has been implemented.
claims.quote: Again, the call is blocked until it's been implemented.
claims.note: 'Again' implies Sam has said the same of another call before; the quote does not name which. The blockquote leaves 'it' unnamed, and Decided item 2 reads 'it' as the separate commodity-search ticket.

claims.statement: Nothing confirming that a transit country has been added or removed is needed where a row of transit countries is added to a table.
claims.ref: ruling-sam-2026-11-10.md blockquote, lines 9-10; restated as the bold sentence of Decided item 3
claims.quote: Don't think you need something confirming a transit country has been added or removed when there's a row of transit countries added to a table.
claims.note: Answers the waiting-on-design question on transit countries in place, design question 4 of the 9 October afternoon ruling, whose transit clause sits in conflict c-006 and whose backlog row is inc-030. The quote carries no JavaScript qualifier; see ruling-sam-2026-11-10-p1-017 and the gap ruling-sam-2026-11-10-p1-022.

claims.statement: The added-countries table is itself the confirmation: a country was there and now is not, or was not there and now is.
claims.ref: ruling-sam-2026-11-10.md blockquote, lines 10-11; restated in Decided item 3
claims.quote: What confirmation do you need other than it was there, now it isn't, or it wasn't there, now it is?
claims.note: Inferred because the blockquote puts it as a rhetorical question rather than a statement; it follows because the question asks what more is needed than the table's own change, and Decided item 3 records it as decided: 'The added-countries table already shows a country appearing or going.'

claims.statement: Germinal products follow live animals and are not a design question.
claims.quote: **Germinal products follow live animals; they are not a design question.**
claims.note: Inferred because the blockquote does not use the words 'not a design question'; it follows from 'I don't think germline suits being in the waiting-on-design thing' together with 'Germlines will just match in with animals as a reference point for everything', the waiting-on-design theme being the theme whose rows wait for design to answer a question.

claims.statement: The germinal dates' 'Choose date' calendar, backlog row inc-192, leaves the waiting-on-design theme.
claims.quote: The germinal dates' 'Choose date' calendar (inc-192) leaves the waiting-on-design theme
claims.note: Inferred because the blockquote names no increment id; it follows from 'I don't think germline suits being in the waiting-on-design thing'. Answers design question 12 of the 9 October afternoon ruling, the germinal dates' calendar, recorded as conflict c-283, whose row is inc-192.

claims.statement: The germinal date calendar work is merged into the germinal identification dates row, backlog row inc-053.
claims.quote: is merged into the germinal identification dates row (inc-053)
claims.note: Inferred because the blockquote names no increment id; it follows from 'fold this in the Germinals date calendar into one of the rows on Germinals, but that doesn't suit being separate'. The blockquote does not say which germinals row, so naming inc-053 is the main session's reading.

claims.statement: The germinal dates are built with the same MOJ date picker the other dates use.
claims.quote: the dates are built with the MOJ date picker the other dates use, as the interaction designer ruled on 9 November.
claims.note: The blockquote is silent on how the dates are built: it names neither the MOJ date picker nor the 9 November ruling, and Decided item 1 cites the interaction designer's 9 November ruling as the authority. So this ruling places the work rather than choosing the component. Verifier and reconciler: take the component from ruling:interaction-designer-2026-11-09, not from this source.

claims.statement: The design call on commodity search listing results as the trader types, backlog row inc-014, stays blocked until the separate commodity-search ticket has been implemented.
claims.quote: The design call on results as you type (inc-014) stays blocked until that ticket has been implemented
claims.note: Inferred because the blockquote names no increment id; it follows from 'Commodities search is being handled by a different ticket. Again, the call is blocked until it's been implemented.' Holds design question 3 of the 9 October afternoon ruling, commodity search as you type, recorded as conflict c-012, whose row is inc-014.

claims.statement: The commodity-search design call does not go to the designer before that ticket has been implemented.
claims.quote: and does not go to the designer before then.
claims.note: Inferred because the blockquote says only that the call is blocked, not who it is kept from; it follows from the call being blocked read against the setting note, which says Sam was reviewing what could be built before the session with the new interaction designer. How far 'the designer' reaches is left open: see the gap ruling-sam-2026-11-10-p1-021.

claims.statement: The joined search button belongs to the separate commodity-search ticket, not to this backlog.
claims.quote: The joined search button and the 'cattle' search listing germinal codes belong to that ticket, not to this backlog.
claims.note: Inferred because the blockquote names neither the joined search button nor this backlog; it follows from 'Commodities search is being handled by a different ticket', the joined search button being part of the commodity search.

claims.statement: A 'cattle' search listing germinal codes belongs to the separate commodity-search ticket, not to this backlog.
claims.quote: The joined search button and the 'cattle' search listing germinal codes belong to that ticket, not to this backlog.
claims.note: Split from ruling-sam-2026-11-10-p1-015, which the Decided item joins with 'and'. Inferred because the blockquote does not mention the 'cattle' search or germinal codes; it follows from commodities search being another ticket's work.

claims.statement: No visible message is shown when a transit country is added or removed without JavaScript.
claims.quote: No visible message is added for an add or remove without JavaScript.
claims.note: Inferred, and narrower than the quote: the blockquote carries no 'without JavaScript' qualifier at all, saying flatly that nothing confirming an add or remove is needed. Decided item 3's qualifier is the main session's reading, so whether the no-message decision also covers a JavaScript-enhanced add or remove is not settled here: see the gap ruling-sam-2026-11-10-p1-022.

claims.statement: These decisions were made by Sam, the owner of the work, while reviewing what in the waiting-on-design theme could be built before the session with the new interaction designer.
claims.quote: Decided by Sam while reviewing what in the waiting-on-design theme could be built before the session with the new interaction designer.
claims.note: Sets how far each decision reaches: the subject is which waiting-on-design rows can be built now, ahead of the interaction designer session, rather than a general ruling on germinal, commodity or transit design.

claims.statement: The ruling does not name which separate ticket handles commodity search, nor where that ticket is tracked.
claims.note: Both the blockquote and Decided item 2 say only 'a different ticket' / 'a separate ticket', so nothing can tell when it is implemented or who owns it.

claims.statement: The ruling does not say who reopens the commodity-search design call once the separate ticket is implemented, or when it is revisited.
claims.note: It says the call stays blocked until that ticket has been implemented, and nothing about what happens then.

claims.statement: The ruling does not say whether keeping the commodity-search call from the designer bars only the session with the new interaction designer or every design route.
claims.ref: ruling-sam-2026-11-10.md claim 2, 'does not go to the designer before then'

claims.statement: The ruling does not say whether the rest of the JavaScript transit-country enhancement is dropped: adding a country the moment it is picked, removing one without a page load, and the 'Added' and 'Removed' announcements.
claims.note: Those three are design question 4's subject, held in conflict c-006 and carried by backlog row inc-030. Decided item 3 settles only the visible message, and only 'without JavaScript', so whether inc-030 is dropped, narrowed or left blocked is open.

claims.statement: The ruling does not say what becomes of the single text input, its 'For example, 27/03/2026' hint and the V4 checks the germinal identification dates row already builds, once the MOJ date picker is merged into that row.
claims.note: It says the calendar is merged into inc-053 and the dates use the MOJ date picker, without saying whether the picker replaces or sits over what inc-053 builds.

claims.statement: The ruling does not say whether the other waiting-on-design rows that touch germinal pages leave the theme alongside the germinal date calendar.
claims.note: The blockquote says germline does not suit being in the waiting-on-design theme in general, while Decided item 1 moves only the germinal date calendar out of it.
